lesson_scope: Algebraic and geometric methods for finding exact Cartesian and polar square roots of complex numbers: equating real and imaginary parts, formulating and solving quartic equations in x or y, rejecting non-real squared roots, surd coefficients, quadratic equations with complex coefficients, polar square roots, and solving biquadratic quartics.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Square roots of pure imaginary number 8i.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding square roots of pure imaginary number.

walkthrough.text:
Equate real and imaginary parts:
$$(x + \mathrm{i}y)^2 = 8\mathrm{i} \implies x^2 - y^2 = 0, \quad 2xy = 8$$

Solve for $x$ and $y$:
$$x^2 = y^2 \implies x = y \quad (\text{since } xy = 4 > 0)$$
$$x^2 = 4 \implies x = \pm 2, \quad y = \pm 2 \implies \text{Roots: } \pm(2 + 2\mathrm{i})$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Square roots of negative pure imaginary number -16i.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding square roots of negative imaginary quantity.

walkthrough.text:
Equate real and imaginary parts:
$$x^2 - y^2 = 0, \quad 2xy = -16 \implies xy = -8$$

Solve for $x$ and $y$:
$$y = -x \implies x^2 = 8 \implies x = \pm 2\sqrt{2}, \quad y = \mp 2\sqrt{2}$$
$$\text{Roots: } \pm(2\sqrt{2} - 2\sqrt{2}\mathrm{i})$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Standard 3-4-5 complex square root.

walkthrough.text:
Form quartic in $x$:
$$x^2 - y^2 = 3, \quad 2xy = 4 \implies y = \frac{2}{x}$$
$$x^2 - \frac{4}{x^2} = 3 \implies x^4 - 3x^2 - 4 = 0$$

Solve for real $x$ and $y$:
$$(x^2 - 4)(x^2 + 1) = 0 \implies x^2 = 4 \implies x = \pm 2, \quad y = \pm 1$$
$$\text{Roots: } \pm(2 + \mathrm{i})$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: 5-12-13 complex square root.

walkthrough.text:
Form quartic in $x$:
$$x^2 - y^2 = 5, \quad 2xy = -12 \implies y = -\frac{6}{x}$$
$$x^2 - \frac{36}{x^2} = 5 \implies x^4 - 5x^2 - 36 = 0$$

Solve for real $x$ and $y$:
$$(x^2 - 9)(x^2 + 4) = 0 \implies x^2 = 9 \implies x = \pm 3, \quad y = \mp 2$$
$$\text{Roots: } \pm(3 - 2\mathrm{i})$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: 7-24-25 complex square root.

walkthrough.text:
Equate real and imaginary parts:
$$x^2 - y^2 = -7, \quad 2xy = 24 \implies y = \frac{12}{x}$$
$$x^2 - \frac{144}{x^2} = -7 \implies x^4 + 7x^2 - 144 = 0$$

Solve for real $x$ and $y$:
$$(x^2 + 16)(x^2 - 9) = 0 \implies x^2 = 9 \implies x = \pm 3, \quad y = \pm 4$$
$$\text{Roots: } \pm(3 + 4\mathrm{i})$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates parts to form $x^2 - y^2 = -7$ and $xy = 12$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Square roots of 8 - 6i and Argand geometry.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Square roots and geometric diametric opposition.

hints: Roots are $\pm(3 - \mathrm{i})$, which are diametrically opposite in the Argand plane.

walkthrough.text:
Solve quartic in $x$:
$$x^4 - 8x^2 - 9 = 0 \implies (x^2 - 9)(x^2 + 1) = 0 \implies x^2 = 9$$
$$x = \pm 3, \quad y = \mp 1 \implies \text{Roots: } \pm(3 - \mathrm{i})$$

Describe geometric relationship:
$$\text{The two roots are diametrically opposite points with respect to the origin (differing by } \pi\text{ radians).}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Derivation of quartic and exact square roots of 21 - 20i.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving quartic equation in x.

walkthrough.text:
Equate real and imaginary parts:
$$(x + \mathrm{i}y)^2 = 21 - 20\mathrm{i} \implies x^2 - y^2 = 21, \quad 2xy = -20 \implies y = -\frac{10}{x}$$

Substitute and form quartic:
$$x^2 - \left(-\frac{10}{x}\right)^2 = 21 \implies x^2 - \frac{100}{x^2} = 21 \implies x^4 - 21x^2 - 100 = 0$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving quartic to obtain roots.

walkthrough.text:
Factorise quartic in $x^2$:
$$(x^2 - 25)(x^2 + 4) = 0 \implies x^2 = 25 \quad (\text{reject } x^2 = -4 \text{ since } x \in \mathbb{R})$$

Calculate $x$ and $y$:
$$x = \pm 5, \quad y = -\frac{10}{\pm 5} = \mp 2 \implies \text{Roots: } \pm(5 - 2\mathrm{i})$$

ai_rubric.observable: Solves quadratic in $x^2$ and explains rejection of $x^2 = -4$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Square roots of -15 + 8i and modulus computation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Forming and solving quartic in x.

walkthrough.text:
Equate real and imaginary parts:
$$x^2 - y^2 = -15, \quad 2xy = 8 \implies y = \frac{4}{x}$$
$$x^2 - \frac{16}{x^2} = -15 \implies x^4 + 15x^2 - 16 = 0$$

Solve for $x^2$:
$$(x^2 + 16)(x^2 - 1) = 0 \implies x^2 = 1 \quad (\text{since } x \in \mathbb{R})$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding square roots and evaluating modulus.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate $x$ and $y$:
$$x = \pm 1, \quad y = \frac{4}{\pm 1} = \pm 4 \implies \text{Roots: } \pm(1 + 4\mathrm{i})$$

Compute root modulus:
$$|\pm(1 + 4\mathrm{i})| = \sqrt{1^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{17}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Square roots of 24 - 7i with rationalised surds.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Forming integer coefficient quartic for square roots of 24 - 7i.

walkthrough.text:
Equate real and imaginary parts:
$$x^2 - y^2 = 24, \quad 2xy = -7 \implies y = -\frac{7}{2x}$$
$$x^2 - \frac{49}{4x^2} = 24 \implies 4x^4 - 96x^2 - 49 = 0$$

Factorise and solve for $x^2$:
$$(2x^2 - 49)(2x^2 + 1) = 0 \implies x^2 = \frac{49}{2} \quad (\text{since } x \in \mathbb{R})$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Expressing square roots with rationalised denominators.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate $x$ with rationalised denominator:
$$x = \pm\sqrt{\frac{49}{2}} = \pm\frac{7}{\sqrt{2}} = \pm\frac{7\sqrt{2}}{2}$$

Calculate $y$ and state roots:
$$y = -\frac{7}{2(\pm 7/\sqrt{2})} = \mp\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \mp\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$$
$$\text{Roots: } \pm\left(\frac{7\sqrt{2}}{2} - \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\mathrm{i}\right)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Square roots of -1 - 4*sqrt(5)*i with surd coefficients.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving quartic equation for surd complex square root.

walkthrough.text:
Equate real and imaginary parts:
$$x^2 - y^2 = -1, \quad 2xy = -4\sqrt{5} \implies y = -\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{x}$$

Substitute into real-part equation:
$$x^2 - \left(-\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{x}\right)^2 = -1 \implies x^2 - \frac{20}{x^2} = -1 \implies x^4 + x^2 - 20 = 0$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving quartic to obtain surd Cartesian square roots.

walkthrough.text:
Factorise and solve for $x^2$:
$$(x^2 + 5)(x^2 - 4) = 0 \implies x^2 = 4 \quad (\text{reject } x^2 = -5 \text{ since } x \in \mathbb{R})$$

Calculate $x$ and $y$:
$$x = \pm 2, \quad y = -\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{\pm 2} = \mp\sqrt{5} \implies \text{Roots: } \pm(2 - \sqrt{5}\,\mathrm{i})$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Square roots of -4 + 6*sqrt(5)*i and solving quadratic equation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding square roots of -4 + 6*sqrt(5)*i via quartic.

walkthrough.text:
Form and solve quartic in $x$:
$$x^2 - y^2 = -4, \quad 2xy = 6\sqrt{5} \implies y = \frac{3\sqrt{5}}{x}$$
$$x^2 - \frac{45}{x^2} = -4 \implies x^4 + 4x^2 - 45 = 0$$
$$(x^2 + 9)(x^2 - 5) = 0 \implies x^2 = 5 \quad (\text{reject } x^2 = -9)$$

Calculate roots:
$$x = \pm\sqrt{5}, \quad y = \frac{3\sqrt{5}}{\pm\sqrt{5}} = \pm 3 \implies \text{Roots: } \pm(\sqrt{5} + 3\mathrm{i})$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving quadratic equation with complex discriminant.

walkthrough.text:
Apply quadratic formula:
$$z = \frac{-2 \pm \sqrt{4 - 4(5 - 6\sqrt{5}\mathrm{i})}}{2} = \frac{-2 \pm \sqrt{-16 + 24\sqrt{5}\mathrm{i}}}{2}$$

Substitute square roots from part (a):
$$\sqrt{-16 + 24\sqrt{5}\mathrm{i}} = 2\sqrt{-4 + 6\sqrt{5}\mathrm{i}} = \pm 2(\sqrt{5} + 3\mathrm{i})$$
$$z = -1 \pm (\sqrt{5} + 3\mathrm{i}) \implies z_1 = (-1 + \sqrt{5}) + 3\mathrm{i}, \quad z_2 = (-1 - \sqrt{5}) - 3\mathrm{i}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Polar versus Cartesian square roots and exact trigonometric values.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Expressing complex number and its square roots in polar form.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate modulus and argument of $w$:
$$r = \sqrt{(-18\sqrt{3})^2 + 18^2} = \sqrt{972 + 324} = 36$$
$$\theta = \pi - \arctan\left(\frac{18}{18\sqrt{3}}\right) = \frac{5\pi}{6} \implies w = 36\mathrm{e}^{\frac{5\pi}{6}\mathrm{i}}$$

Find square roots in polar form:
$$z = \pm\sqrt{36}\,\mathrm{e}^{\frac{5\pi}{12}\mathrm{i}} = \pm 6\mathrm{e}^{\frac{5\pi}{12}\mathrm{i}}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Deducing exact values of cos(5pi/12) and sin(5pi/12).

walkthrough.text:
Solve system $x^2 + y^2 = 36$ and $x^2 - y^2 = -18\sqrt{3}$:
$$2x^2 = 36 - 18\sqrt{3} \implies x^2 = 18 - 9\sqrt{3}$$
$$2y^2 = 36 + 18\sqrt{3} \implies y^2 = 18 + 9\sqrt{3}$$

Deduce exact trigonometric values:
$$\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right) = \frac{x}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{18 - 9\sqrt{3}}}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}}{4}$$
$$\sin\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right) = \frac{y}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{18 + 9\sqrt{3}}}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Complete quartic formulation, square root finding, and biquadratic quartic solution.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving quartic equation in x.

walkthrough.text:
Equate real and imaginary parts:
$$(x + \mathrm{i}y)^2 = 32 - 24\mathrm{i} \implies x^2 - y^2 = 32, \quad 2xy = -24 \implies y = -\frac{12}{x}$$

Form quartic in $x$:
$$x^2 - \left(-\frac{12}{x}\right)^2 = 32 \implies x^2 - \frac{144}{x^2} = 32 \implies x^4 - 32x^2 - 144 = 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates real parts to get $x^2 - y^2 = 32$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving quartic to obtain exact roots.

walkthrough.text:
Solve for real $x^2$:
$$(x^2 - 36)(x^2 + 4) = 0 \implies x^2 = 36 \quad (\text{reject } x^2 = -4)$$

Calculate $x$ and $y$:
$$x = \pm 6, \quad y = -\frac{12}{\pm 6} = \mp 2 \implies \text{Roots: } \pm(6 - 2\mathrm{i})$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving biquadratic quartic with complex roots.

walkthrough.text:
Solve for $u^2$:
$$u^2 = \frac{64 \pm \sqrt{4096 - 6400}}{2} = \frac{64 \pm 48\mathrm{i}}{2} = 32 \pm 24\mathrm{i}$$

Find square roots of $32 \pm 24\mathrm{i}$:
$$\sqrt{32 - 24\mathrm{i}} = \pm(6 - 2\mathrm{i}), \quad \sqrt{32 + 24\mathrm{i}} = \pm(6 + 2\mathrm{i})$$
$$\text{Four roots: } \pm(6 - 2\mathrm{i}) \text{ and } \pm(6 + 2\mathrm{i})$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses part (b) and conjugate root property to find square roots of both values.
